historySource.name: The National Parks: Index 2012–2016 (National Park Service)
historySource.indexText: This memorial preserves the site of the deadliest home front disaster of World War II, honoring those who lost their lives or were affected by the munitions explosion on July 17, 1944. The disaster and its aftermath illuminated the issues of segregation and revealed inequality in the military. Today the memorial serves as a springboard for exploring social justice in our society. Authorized Oct. 28, 1992. Established Oct. 28, 2009.
